title: Regular ring maps respect ring equivalences
statement: For commutative rings R1, R2, S1, S2 in possibly different universes, maps f : R1 to S1 and g : R2 to S2, and ring equivalences a : R1 \simeq R2 and b : S1 \simeq S2 satisfying b composed with f = g composed with a, regularity [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of f implies regularity of g.

source.place: Definition 07BZ; algebra.tex Lemma 0381, finite purely inseparable criterion

proof.text: Write g = b composed with f composed with a inverse. Flatness of equivalences and composition transports the flat clause.

Pull back a prime of R2 to R1. Mathlib residueFieldRingEquiv identifies residue fields compatibly with the base maps. Semilinear tensor congruence gives a ring equivalence of fibres and their residue-field actions.

Transport Noetherianity. Pull back each finite purely inseparable field extension through the residue-field equivalence, using Module.Finite.trans and IsPurelyInseparable.trans. Module.Finite.small and Shrink provide a model in the original criterion universe. Tensor congruence transports regularity of the base-changed fibre. Apply the defining regular-map criterion.

proof_origin.place: Definition 07BZ; algebra.tex Lemma 0381, finite purely inseparable criterion
proof_origin.note: E2 wrote the transport argument from the definitions and Mathlib universal properties.

mathlib_searches.query: regular ring homomorphism invariant under isomorphism
Regularity of a ring homomorphism is invariant under isomorphisms of its source and target rings
mathlib_searches.results: RingHom.RespectsIso and tools for other properties, no regular-map result.
Only regular elements and Lean reducibility hints, not regular ring maps.

mathlib_searches.query: IsRegular.*[Ee]quiv|IsGeometricallyRegular.*equiv in Mathlib and both library roots
mathlib_searches.results: No existing regular-map or geometric-regularity transport; Flat.comp and IsRegularRing.of_ringEquiv are used.

lean.statement:
theorem RingHom.IsRegular.of_ringEquiv
    {R₁ : Type u₁} {R₂ : Type u₂} {S₁ : Type v₁} {S₂ : Type v₂}
    [CommRing R₁] [CommRing R₂] [CommRing S₁] [CommRing S₂]
    (f : R₁ →+* S₁) (g : R₂ →+* S₂) (a : R₁ ≃+* R₂) (b : S₁ ≃+* S₂)
    (h : b.toRingHom.comp f = g.comp a.toRingHom) (hf : f.IsRegular) :
    g.IsRegular
